newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-CalEnergy dropping $1.9 billion bid for NYSEG.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CalEnergy dropping $1.9 billion bid for NYSEG.

text.p: Independent power producer CalEnergy Co. Inc. said on Friday it dropped its $1.9 billion bid to acquire New York State Electric & Gas Corp. due to lack of support from NYSEG shareholders.

CalEnergy said a $159 million tender offer launched in July to acquire 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares was undersubscribed. The tender was the first step in its effort to acquire the whole company in a deal valued at $1.9 billion.
In a strongly worded statement, the Omaha, Neb.-based power company accused NYSEG's management of undermining its bid.
"We believe NYSEG's frivolous and unrelenting litigation efforts and misinformation campaign unfortunately resulted in the NYSEG shareholders' decision not to accept our offer," the company said.
"We intend to evaluate our options and explore other potential combinations," it added.

NYSEG said it was pleased shareholders showed their support for the company's board by rejecting the tender offer. In a two-sentence statement, the utility also said it is eager to start building on a recent agreement with state regulators to reduce customer prices and build shareholder value.
NYSEG has said the agreement will give it greater flexibility for expansion and has said it will soon review its dividend policy and stock buyback program.
Minimum conditions of the tender offer, which expired at midnight EDT, were not met, CalEnergy said. The tender offer was valued at $24.50 a share.

NYSEG shares were trading slightly above $21 before CalEnergy made its offer, and fell 75 cents to $24.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon Friday. CalEnergy rose 12.5 cents to $35.50 amid broad declines on the NYSE.

Binghamton, N.Y.-based NYSEG had urged holders not to tender their shares and refused to sit down at the negotiating table, saying the offer did not reflect the value of the company. CalEnergy launched its bid July 15 and had said it would be willing to pay $27.50 a share in a negotiated deal.

CalEnergy Chief Executive Officer David Sokol said he would not make another bid for NYSEG and would sell any shares it held. Some traders had speculated he might make another run for the utility in the future.
"We don't think the company is worth $24.50 (per share) without a significant management and strategy change so we are in fact selling our shares that we did own," he said in a telephone interview.
Sokol did not specify how many shares are currently held, but said CalEnergy had owned 250,000 of NYSEG's 69 million outstanding shares.
He said he got the sense earlier in the week that the tender offer was running into trouble.
"I don't want to make excuses. One thing I believe strongly is that shareholders should always be given the right to make a decision. They've made their decision here and we respect that," he said.
However, he cited market expectations that CalEnergy would raise the $24.50 tender offer, and also accused NYSEG of confusing the process with litigation and appeals to state regulators.
Industry analysts said CalEnergy was expected to rebound quickly from the failed effort and had plenty of opportunities to acquire another utility.
"I think the company has demonstrated they are disciplined acquirers," said Ali Agha of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
Sokol said the company is eager to pursue other transactions, saying that it would potentially launch another unsolicited effort even though it would prefer a friendly deal.

"We would always choose a friendly transaction, if possible, over a hostile one, but we would be prepared to pursue a transaction if necessary thorugh an unsolicited offer if that was the only way we could get it to the shareholders," he said.
He declined to comment on the region that CalEnergy finds appealing, saying that the company frequently is involved in discussions about potential transactions.
"We think there are 20 to 30 different U.S. utilities which would allow us to achieve our goals here in the U.S.," Sokol said, adding it also is pursuing growth in Asia and Europe.
Analysts have said that CalEnergy will likely pursue a transaction in the Northeast and recently has indicated interest in the southwestern part of the country.
